words.ex: Aziz spent so long in the bird house at the zoo that he never reached the large mammals: the bears, the bison and the camels.
Kamila's favourite moment in the Australian nature film was a baby wallaby peeping out of its mother's pouch; she had never seen marsupials before.
The farmer keeps two cats in the barn to protect the grain from mice and other rodents.
On our school trip to the desert, the guide showed us where snakes, lizards and other reptiles hide from the midday heat.
Our cat is a carnivore, so the vet told us not to put it on a vegetarian diet.
The keeper explained that the goats in the petting zoo are herbivores, so visitors may only feed them carrots and hay.
Small birds stay close to the bushes so that they can hide quickly from predators such as hawks.
After the wolves had finished eating, the scavengers arrived: a flock of crows and a pair of vultures picked the bones clean.
Watching the sparrows hop about in the snow, Malika wondered how such tiny warm-blooded creatures keep going on freezing mornings.
Our class tortoise barely moves until the radiator warms the room; being cold-blooded, it can't produce enough heat of its own.
The pony at the riding school is so docile that even five-year-olds can ride it safely.
The pigeons in the square have become so tame that they take seeds straight from visitors' hands.
Our biology teacher asked us to name animals that people have domesticated, and Jasur surprised everyone by adding silkworms to the list.
The documentary showed a savage fight between two male bears that left both of them badly injured.
The neighbours' dog looks fierce when it barks at passers-by, but it is actually very friendly once you know it.
When the old woodland by the river was cut down for a car park, the owls and hedgehogs lost their natural habitat.
Every autumn, thousands of cranes migrate south over the mountains to spend the winter in warmer lands.
Scientists fitted tiny GPS trackers to the storks to follow their migration from Europe to Africa.
Ostriches may be flightless, but on the farm we visited one easily outran the owner's motorbike.
In the museum we saw a model of a mammoth, an animal that became extinct thousands of years ago.
On their trip to Kenya, they spent three days in a game reserve, watching lions and elephants from a jeep.
The old fish ponds have been turned into a bird sanctuary, where pelicans and herons can nest safely.
Instead of buying a puppy, we adopted a dog from the local animal shelter.
Mr Rakhimov in the flat below still types letters on a typewriter and refuses to own a mobile; he's a real dodo when it comes to technology.
In the class debate, most of us argued that bullfighting, foxhunting and other blood sports should be banned.
The designer has stopped using real fur, saying she no longer wants to support the fur trade.
Rangers in the national park now use drones with night cameras to spot poachers in the dark.
The documentary showed how elephant tusks are secretly sent across the world to supply the illegal ivory trade.
A group of animal rights activists collected signatures against keeping dolphins in small pools.
The old ram at the edge of the flock had one horn that curled almost into a full circle.
In the nineteenth century, wealthy landowners kept large forests where deer, pheasants and other game were raised for hunting.
The horses on the steppe look like farm animals, but they are completely wild and run off whenever a car comes near.
Every evening the woman at the corner bakery leaves a bowl of milk by the door for the stray cats that nobody owns.
On the island of Mauritius, sailors hunted the dodo, a large bird that could not fly, while the rats and pigs they brought ate its eggs.
